title: Create a self-contained Linux release bundle for GitHub releases
description: The new GitHub Actions release workflow can build Linux and publish an installed-tree tarball, but xSTUDIO still lacks a proper Linux release packaging path comparable to the existing Windows NSIS installer and macOS zip bundle. Add a dedicated Linux release artifact format (for example AppImage or a distro-neutral runtime bundle) that includes the required Qt/runtime dependencies for end-user distribution. This was discovered while implementing xstudio-j84.

title: Validate macOS notarization flow with live release credentials
description: The xstudio_macos_zip/xstudio_macos_notarize release tooling is now in place, but this machine does not have a live Developer ID identity or Apple notarization credentials available for an end-to-end release submission. Track the first credentialed release/CI run so we can verify the final Apple-side notarization path and capture any entitlements or CI keychain setup adjustments that are still needed.

title: Clean up remaining CMake developer warnings during configure
description: macOS configure/build is functionally clean after the app-bundle fix, but CMake still emits developer warnings from top-level NSIS string quoting in CMakeLists.txt and CMP0177 install-destination warnings from bundled OpenTimelineIO/vcpkg integration. Track a separate cleanup so local configure output is quieter and easier to trust.

title: Set up release macOS signing and notarization for app bundles
description: Local macOS builds now produce a runnable xSTUDIO.app that passes standard strict codesign verification after a normal build. Remaining release work is to establish Developer ID signing and Apple notarization for distributable bundles, including any entitlements, signing identities, and CI/release automation needed for shipping artifacts.
close_reason: Implemented macOS release signing/notarization targets and documentation

title: Validate Filesystem Browser UNC sequence loading on Windows runtime
description: Follow up on xstudio-mie after the browser sequence-load path refactor. Run the Filesystem Browser on a real Windows machine against an actual UNC share and verify that loading sequence items no longer lands in a "media not found" state. Confirm at least these cases: `//server/share/my_file.####.exr`, `//server/share/my_file_%04d.exr`, and underscore-containing basenames. Capture any remaining URI/CAF edge cases if runtime behaviour still differs from the local unit-tested normalization logic.

title: Document macOS app bundle deploy/sign behavior
description: Add a short note to the macOS build guide covering the current post-build app bundle flow: normal builds run macdeployqt, scrub build/Homebrew rpaths from the .app bundle, prefer the bundled ffmpeg for the filesystem browser plugin, and use relaxed codesign verification for local launch. Include the remaining notarization follow-up as a pointer to xstudio-ulg.

title: Add GitHub Actions multi-platform release builds
description: Create a GitHub Actions workflow that builds xSTUDIO on native Windows, Linux, and macOS runners and publishes artifacts for release automation. The workflow should support release-triggered uploads, use the repo's existing CMake/package entry points where practical, and document any remaining signing/notarization follow-up separately.

title: Fix Filesystem Browser loading of UNC image sequences on Windows
description:
Filesystem Browser on Windows can produce media that immediately lands in a "media not found" state when loading sequence items from UNC shares. Repro context from user report: browsing/loading a path like `//server/share/myfile_%04d.exr` from the Filesystem Browser results in a media item whose Media tab says "media not found".

Updated investigation:
- The browser already contains sequence-format conversion work: when it successfully parses a sequence with `fileseq`, it converts the browser path to xSTUDIO brace syntax before calling `playlist.add_media(...)` (see `src/plugin/python_plugins/filesystem_browser/filesystem_browser.py`). So the earlier printf/brace fix is real.
- The bug is more likely in the Filesystem Browser code path than in the core EXR reader. The browser currently has two different media-add implementations:
  - `load_file()` contains older inline sequence handling and only converts to brace syntax when `len(seq) > 1`.
  - `_add_media_to_playlist()` contains newer helper logic and converts whenever `fileseq` returns a usable `frameSet()`.
- Because the logic is duplicated, the single-item browser load path can fall back to sending a raw path/template to `playlist.add_media(path)` instead of the normalized brace+range form. That would explain why the media item is created but later reports "media not found".
- UNC handling is still part of the risk surface. The browser normalizes many paths to forward-slash form (`//server/share/...`), and this needs explicit validation end-to-end in the browser load path, not just in core helpers.
- `%04d` support is still worth preserving/checking, but it is secondary here. The browser is supposed to normalize sequence paths before they hit core parsing.
- Underscores do not look like the primary problem. Existing sequence logic appears compatible with basenames like `my_file.####.exr`; the existing intentional exception is version-style `_v001` handling.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Loading a sequence item from the Filesystem Browser on Windows from a UNC share (for example `//server/share/...`) no longer results in Media tab status "media not found".
2. The browser uses a single shared sequence-to-xSTUDIO conversion path for single-file load, multi-load, compare, preview, and timeline insert, rather than duplicated divergent logic.
3. Verify the packaged/runtime browser path still has `fileseq` available on Windows, or fail loudly instead of silently falling back to raw template paths.
4. Add coverage for UNC browser paths and underscore-containing sequence basenames such as `//server/share/my_file.####.exr`.
5. Keep `%04d` compatibility as a secondary check so the prior printf work is not regressed.
close_reason: Implemented the Filesystem Browser sequence-load path refactor, unified single-item loads on the shared normalization helper, and added UNC/underscore-focused path normalization tests. Follow-up Windows runtime validation is tracked separately in xstudio-d6e.

title: Fix macOS app bundle retaining absolute Homebrew Qt framework paths
description: After `cmake --build build --target install` on macOS, `build/xSTUDIO.app/Contents/MacOS/xstudio.bin` still contains absolute /opt/homebrew Qt framework install names (QtCore/QtGui/QtWidgets/QtQml/QtNetwork/QtOpenGL/QtDBus/QtSvg/QtTest). Launching the rebuilt app then loads both bundled Qt and Homebrew Qt, causing duplicate-class warnings and Cocoa platform plugin failures until the binary is manually patched with install_name_tool. Investigate why install/fixup/macdeployqt is leaving these references behind and make the bundle runnable without manual post-build surgery.

title: Prepare 1.1.3 release notes and publish the 1.1.3 GitHub release
description: Update xSTUDIO to version 1.1.3, refresh the startup release-notes content so the launch dialog shows the current release highlights, and publish the 1.1.3 GitHub release so the multi-platform release workflow runs against a real release tag.

title: Investigate strict macOS codesign/notarization for app bundle
description: The rebuilt macOS xSTUDIO.app now launches correctly without manual install_name_tool surgery after bundle rpath cleanup and post-build macdeployqt/fixup. However, bundle-level codesign still needs --ignore-resources because QML/plugin resource directories inside the app bundle look like nested bundles to codesign. Track a follow-up to make the bundle verify cleanly under standard macOS codesign/notarization flows without the relaxed ignore-resources path.

title: Fix macOS viewport drag-drop not updating transport/playhead state
description: Dragging video/image sequence media directly into the viewport on macOS plays in the viewport, but the transport bar stays stale: controls are not interactive, frame counter does not increment, and transport state does not follow the dropped media. Reported for EXR and MOV. Investigate drag-drop path, viewport/playhead attachment, and transport model synchronization.
close_reason: Fixed viewport and transport playhead sync
